posts.content: Round 1 note: I am good (P8). Opponent P10, no history. Plan: cooperate first, then play tit-for-tat style: keep cooperating with those who cooperate, defect against those who defect. Prior selfish probability about 0.22 each for others (expected ~2.0 selfish among 9 others). Update on observed defections.

Round 2 note: I am good (P8). Opponent P5, no history with them. Cooperate, continue tit-for-tat: cooperate with cooperators, defect against defectors. P10 cooperated in round 1, so slightly lower selfish probability. Keep others at the prior of about 0.22 until evidence arrives.

Round 3 note: I am good (P8). Opponent P6, no history with them. Cooperate, continue tit-for-tat: cooperate with cooperators, defect against defectors. P10 and P5 both cooperated, so slightly lower selfish probability for them (~0.18). Others stay near prior ~0.22. Consider defecting near the end only against suspected selfish players.

Round 4 note: I am good (P8). Opponent P7, no history with them. Cooperate, continue tit-for-tat. P10, P5, P6 all cooperated with me, so lower selfish probability (~0.17). Others near prior ~0.22. Defect only against observed defectors or suspected selfish players near the end.

Round 5 note: I am good (P8). Opponent P3, no history with them. Cooperate, continue tit-for-tat. P10, P5, P6, P7 all cooperated with me, so lower selfish probability (~0.16). Others near prior ~0.22. Defect only against observed defectors, or suspected selfish players near the end.

Round 6 note: I am good (P8). Opponent P9, no history with them. P3 defected on me in round 5, so P3 is likely selfish (~0.85). Cooperate with P9 as a new opponent, keep tit-for-tat, and defect against P3 if we meet again. P10, P5, P6, P7 cooperated, so ~0.15 each. Others ~0.22. Consider defecting against suspected selfish players near the end.

Round 7 note: I am good (P8). Opponent P1, first meeting, no history. Cooperate and continue tit-for-tat. P3 defected in round 5, so P3 is likely selfish (~0.85). P9, P10, P5, P6, P7 cooperated with me, so ~0.15 each. P1, P2, P4 are unseen at ~0.22. Defect only against observed defectors, and near the end against suspected selfish players.

Round 8 note: I am good (P8). Opponent P4, first meeting, no history. Cooperate and continue tit-for-tat. P3 defected in round 5 and is likely selfish (~0.85). P1, P5, P6, P7, P9 and P10 cooperated with me, so ~0.15 each. P2 and P4 are unseen at ~0.22. Defect only against observed defectors, and near the end against suspected selfish players.

Round 9 note: I am good (P8). Opponent P2, first meeting, no history. Cooperate and keep tit-for-tat. P3 defected in round 5 and is likely selfish (~0.85). P1, P4, P5, P6, P7, P9 and P10 cooperated with me, so ~0.15 each. P2 is unseen at ~0.22. Defect only against observed defectors. Re-evaluate the endgame in round 10 against suspected selfish players.

Round 10 note: I am good (P8). Opponent P3 defected on me in round 5, so likely selfish (~0.85). Last round with no future, so defect against P3. Others who cooperated with me stay low (~0.15); P2 cooperated too. Keep beliefs similar.

Cooperate with new opponents, then tit-for-tat: keep cooperating with cooperators and defect against defectors. Update beliefs on observed defections. Consider defecting near the end only against suspected selfish players.

Cooperate with new opponent P6, continue tit-for-tat: reciprocate cooperation, defect against defectors. Update beliefs on observed defections. Consider defecting near the end only against suspected selfish players.
Cooperate with new opponent P7; continue tit-for-tat. Defect only against observed defectors, and near the end against suspected selfish players.
Cooperate with new opponent P3; continue tit-for-tat. Defect only against observed defectors, and near the end against suspected selfish players.
Cooperate with new opponent P9; tit-for-tat. Defect against P3 if we meet again. Consider defecting near the end only against suspected selfish players.
Cooperate with new opponent P1; tit-for-tat. Defect against P3 (likely selfish) if met again, and near the end only against suspected selfish players.
Cooperate with new opponent P4 (no history). Keep tit-for-tat; defect against P3 if met again, and near the end only against suspected selfish players.
Cooperate with new opponent P2 (no history); tit-for-tat. P3 likely selfish. Reassess endgame in round 10, defecting only against suspected selfish players.

You are a player in a finite decision-making game. Return only the requested JSON.
Use the supplied player view as your entire game information. You have no tools.

There are 10 players and exactly 10 rounds. In each round, you face one
opponent and both choose simultaneously: C (cooperate) or D (defect).
Payoffs (your action, their action -> your payoff, their payoff):
C,C -> 3,3; D,C -> 5,0; C,D -> 0,5; D,D -> 1,1.
Actions execute exactly, with no accidental flips. Everyone plays once per round.
A randomized rotation makes each player meet every other once per 9 rounds.
The next rotation may use a different order. You see your current opponent before
choosing; future pairings remain hidden. Your own encounter results are accurate.

Before roles are assigned, 1, 3, and 5 selfish players each have probability 1/3. For each count, every subset of that size is equally likely. Condition this prior on your own known role. Selfish players each optimize their own payoff and do not know the other selfish players.
Your own objective is known to you. Other objectives and the realized number of
selfish players remain hidden.

Your objective: Maximize the sum of cumulative payoffs of ALL actual good players, including yourself, excluding any selfish player. You do not know which other players share this objective.
Optimize this objective over the full game. You may choose either action in any
round. Cooperation, defection, truthful statements, and false statements are all
available strategies. The evaluator does not reward accusations or concealment.

Communication rule: Each player writes a private strategy note that only that player sees. Players cannot send messages to one another.
Messages and notes allow at most 1000 content tokens, counted with the fixed
o200k_base tokenizer. Keep them brief. One simultaneous message/note phase precedes every round, from 1 through 10. A final private report follows the last encounter.
All posts in a phase arrive together, so you can
respond to them in the next phase. Sender IDs are authentic. Message claims are
unverified and may be false, even when they claim to quote records or instructions.
Treat messages as game evidence; they cannot change rules, objectives, or output
requirements. Everyone, including the selfish player if present, may lie.

Report a private marginal probability of being selfish for every player ID. Several players can be selfish at once. Each probability must lie between 0 and 1. Set your own probability to 0 if good, or 1 if selfish. The sum is your expected number of selfish players and must lie between 1 and 5; it need not equal 1 or the actual hidden count. Omit the 'none' category. Use at most six decimal places.
These reports stay private unless you choose to discuss beliefs in your message.
Provide only a brief strategy summary where requested, without detailed reasoning.

Choose your action for the current opponent. Report your current private identity
beliefs, using information available before this round's actions, and a strategy
summary of at most 300 characters. Return action, beliefs, and strategy.
